::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## TL;DR

Superficial temporal artery to middle cerebral artery ($\text{STA-MCA}$) bypass rescues ischemic brains from stroke, but sudden high-pressure reperfusion into paralyzed capillaries can trigger fatal Cerebral Hyperperfusion Syndrome ($\text{CHS}$). By acquiring intraoperative Perfusion-Weighted MRI ($\text{PWI-MRI}$) on the surgical table immediately following microvascular anastomosis, we demonstrate that a relative cerebral blood flow surge ($>150\%$) combined with rapid transit shortening predicts impending hyperperfusion with $87.5\%$ sensitivity and $92.3\%$ specificity—enabling life-saving blood pressure intervention before hemorrhage occurs.
:::

---

## 1. The Clinical Dilemma: Ischemia vs. Hyperperfusion

In patients with advanced **Moyamoya disease** or severe intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis, chronically starved brain tissue survives in a state of maximal autoregulatory vasodilation:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    ChronicStenosis["Severe Carotid / MCA Stenosis<br/>Chronic Cerebral Ischemia"] --> Autoregulation["Maximal Compensatory Vasodilation<br/>Capillary Autoregulation Lost"]
    Autoregulation --> BypassSurgery["STA-MCA Microvascular Bypass<br/>Direct Arterial Blood Flow Restored"]
    
    BypassSurgery --> PathGood["Optimal Perfusion Restored<br/>Brain Tissue Rescued from Stroke"]
    BypassSurgery --> PathCHS["Massive Sudden Inflow (Hyperperfusion)<br/>Damaged Vessels Cannot Constrict"]
    
    PathCHS --> CapillaryBreakdown["Blood-Brain Barrier Rupture & Vasogenic Edema"]
    CapillaryBreakdown --> Hemorrhage["Fatal Intracerebral Hemorrhage (CHS)"]

    class ChronicStenosis rust
    class BypassSurgery indigo
    class PathGood olive
    class PathCHS sienna
    class Hemorrhage terracotta
    classDef indigo fill:#1d4a62,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef sienna fill:#6c2b27,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef rust fill:#a04b2d,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef olive fill:#5b6e34,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef terracotta fill:#c97d62,stroke:#3b1a18,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#3b1a18
```

When a neurosurgeon grafts the superficial temporal artery to the middle cerebral artery ($\text{STA-MCA}$), high-pressure systemic blood suddenly floods these fragile, paralyzed microvessels. If the hyperemic flow exceeds the capillary threshold, **Cerebral Hyperperfusion Syndrome (CHS)** ensues within $24–72\text{ hours}$, causing seizures, severe focal deficits, and deadly hemorrhage[^1].

---

## 2. Quantitative Perfusion-Weighted MRI (PWI) Physics

**Perfusion-Weighted MRI (PWI)** utilizes a rapid bolus injection of paramagnetic gadolinium-based contrast agent while continuously acquiring ultrafast $T_2^*$-weighted echo-planar images. As the contrast bolus passes through brain capillaries, it induces microscopic magnetic field gradients that drop the local signal intensity:

<figcaption><strong>Figure 1 | Hyperperfusion is legible in the shape of the signal drop, not in its presence.</strong> Gadolinium dephases spins in the capillary bed, so $T_2^*$-weighted signal falls as the bolus passes and the tracer concentration is recovered as $C(t) = -(k/\text{TE})\ln[S(t)/S_0]$. In the chronically ischemic hemisphere (blue) collateral flow arrives late and dispersed: time-to-peak is delayed to about $19.8\text{ s}$ and the drop is blunted to roughly $25\%$, the classic signature of exhausted autoregulatory reserve. After $\text{STA-MCA}$ bypass the same voxels deliver an early, sharp, deep bolus (magenta) — TTP near $12.5\text{ s}$ and $\Delta S \approx 50\%$ — because $\text{CBF} = \text{CBV}/\text{MTT}$ has risen while the paralyzed vessels still cannot constrict. It is that abrupt narrowing and deepening, appearing within $24\text{–}72\text{ hours}$, that flags impending hyperperfusion syndrome.</figcaption>
</figure>

The tracer concentration $C(t)$ is calculated from the signal drop:

$$C(t) = -\frac{k}{\text{TE}} \ln \left( \frac{S(t)}{S_0} \right)$$

Using the central volume principle and singular value deconvolution ($\text{SVD}$)[^2], we compute three fundamental hemodynamic parameters:

$$\text{CBF} = \frac{\text{CBV}}{\text{MTT}}$$

1. **Cerebral Blood Volume ($\text{CBV}$)**: Total volume of blood within a given voxel ($C(t)$ area under curve).
2. **Mean Transit Time ($\text{MTT}$)**: Average time for blood to traverse the capillary bed from arterial input to venous outflow.
3. **Time-to-Peak ($\text{TTP}$)**: Time required for the contrast concentration to reach maximum.

---

## 3. The Intraoperative Diagnostic Breakthrough

Historically, hyperperfusion was diagnosed *after* surgery when symptoms appeared, or via post-operative SPECT scans days later.

In our clinical study published in *Scientific Reports*[^3], we utilized a dedicated **intraoperative 1.5T MRI suite**, scanning patients on the surgical table immediately following microvascular bypass completion.

### Key Quantitative Indicators of CHS:

| Hemodynamic Parameter | Normal Successful Bypass | Impending CHS Signature | Diagnostic Utility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Regional CBF Ratio ($\text{rCBF}_{\text{post}} / \text{rCBF}_{\text{pre}}$)** | $1.15–1.35\times$ | **$\ge 1.65\times$ ($+65\%$ surge)** | Strongest amplitude predictor |
| **Regional MTT Ratio ($\text{rMTT}_{\text{post}} / \text{rMTT}_{\text{pre}}$)** | $0.75–0.90\times$ | **$\le 0.55\times$ (Hyper-fast transit)** | Indicates paralyzed, open vessels |
| **TTP Delay Elimination ($\Delta \text{TTP}$)** | Normalized by $1–2\text{ s}$ | **Negative / Abrupt over-clearing** | Loss of vascular resistance |
| **ROC Area Under Curve (AUC)** | — | **$\text{AUC} = 0.941$** | High clinical discrimination |

---

```{=html}
<script>
function updateMriSim() {
  const cbfSurge = parseFloat(document.getElementById('sim-cbf').value);
  const mttRatio = parseFloat(document.getElementById('sim-mtt').value);
  const ischLevel = parseInt(document.getElementById('sim-isch').value);

  document.getElementById('cbf-val').innerText = '+' + cbfSurge + '%';
  document.getElementById('mtt-val').innerText = mttRatio.toFixed(2);
  document.getElementById('isch-val').innerText = ischLevel === 1 ? 'Mild' : (ischLevel === 2 ? 'Moderate' : 'Severe');

  // Logistic regression model risk calculation
  const z = -4.5 + (cbfSurge / 100) * 3.8 - (mttRatio - 0.7) * 4.2 + (ischLevel - 1) * 1.2;
  const prob = 1.0 / (1.0 + Math.exp(-z));
  const probPct = (prob * 100).toFixed(1);

  document.getElementById('chs-bar').style.width = probPct + '%';

  const probEl = document.getElementById('chs-prob');
  const barEl = document.getElementById('chs-bar');
  const recomEl = document.getElementById('chs-recom');

  if (prob < 0.25) {
    probEl.innerText = probPct + '% (Low Risk)';
    probEl.style.color = '#10b981';
    barEl.style.background = '#10b981';
    recomEl.style.background = 'rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.1)';
    recomEl.style.borderLeftColor = '#10b981';
    recomEl.innerText = '✅ Standard post-operative protocol: Maintain normotensive blood pressure (SBP 120–140 mmHg). Continue routine neuro-ICU monitoring.';
  } else if (prob < 0.60) {
    probEl.innerText = probPct + '% (Moderate Risk - Alert)';
    probEl.style.color = '#f59e0b';
    barEl.style.background = '#f59e0b';
    recomEl.style.background = 'rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.1)';
    recomEl.style.borderLeftColor = '#f59e0b';
    recomEl.innerText = '⚠️ Moderate CHS Warning: Initiate strict blood pressure control (SBP < 130 mmHg). Administer free radical scavengers and perform serial follow-up PWI.';
  } else {
    probEl.innerText = probPct + '% (Critical CHS Emergency)';
    probEl.style.color = '#ef4444';
    barEl.style.background = '#ef4444';
    recomEl.style.background = 'rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.1)';
    recomEl.style.borderLeftColor = '#ef4444';
    recomEl.innerText = '🚨 Critical CHS Danger: Aggressive pharmacologic sedation, strict intensive hypotensive management (SBP 100–120 mmHg), and continuous propofol suppression to prevent catastrophic intracerebral hemorrhage.';
  }
}
window.addEventListener('load', updateMriSim);
setTimeout(updateMriSim, 300);
</script>
```


---

## 5. Clinical Impact on Surgical Practice

1. **Zero-Delay Intervention**: By establishing diagnosis *during surgery* rather than waiting for post-operative clinical deterioration, clinical teams can initiate aggressive hypotensive management (e.g., continuous labetalol/nicardipine infusions) before capillary endothelium fails.
2. **Personalized Target Blood Pressure**: Patients with severe pre-operative hemodynamic exhaustion and large intraoperative $\text{rCBF}$ surges receive customized strict systolic blood pressure targets ($<120\text{ mmHg}$), completely eliminating hemorrhagic stroke complications in high-risk cohorts.

---

## Data and Code Availability

- **Clinical Protocols**: Surgical procedures and intraoperative MRI acquisition sequences follow the Prince of Wales Hospital and Huashan Hospital neurovascular guidelines.
- **Statistical Pipeline**: ROC curve analyses and transit parameter deconvolution algorithms were implemented in MATLAB and R.
